title: Classical Time-Series Models
desc: The statistical backbone under every later forecasting method — trend, seasonality and autoregression.

items.name: ARIMA / ARMA
items.desc: Box–Jenkins autoregressive–moving-average models for stationary return series.

items.name: Holt–Winters Exponential Smoothing
items.desc: Recursively weighted trend and seasonality forecasting.

items.name: VAR (Vector Autoregression)
items.desc: Models several interdependent series jointly, each as a function of all series' own lags.

items.name: VECM
items.desc: VAR extended for series that are individually non-stationary but jointly cointegrated.

items.name: SARIMAX
items.desc: ARIMA with seasonal terms and exogenous regressors, e.g. macro variables.

items.name: Kalman Filter (state-space)
items.desc: Recursive Bayesian estimation of an unobserved state, e.g. a time-varying beta.

title: Volatility Models
desc: Conditional-variance models — the input every VaR, option and risk-parity calculation depends on.

items.name: ARCH
items.desc: Engle's model: today's variance depends on yesterday's squared residual.

items.name: GARCH(1,1)
items.desc: Bollerslev's generalised ARCH — the industry-standard volatility workhorse.

items.name: EGARCH
items.desc: Captures the leverage effect: volatility reacts asymmetrically to positive and negative shocks.

items.name: GJR-GARCH
items.desc: Threshold GARCH variant modelling the leverage effect via an explicit indicator term.

items.name: Realized Volatility (RV)
items.desc: Estimates volatility from summed squared high-frequency intraday returns.

items.name: Heston Stochastic Volatility
items.desc: Volatility follows its own stochastic process rather than a deterministic function of past returns.

items.name: HAR-RV
items.desc: Regresses realized volatility on its own daily, weekly and monthly averages.

title: Factor & Asset-Pricing Models
desc: What ‘normal’ expected return looks like — the baseline every anomaly and mispricing is measured against.

items.name: CAPM
items.desc: Single-factor model: expected return is driven by market beta alone.

items.name: Fama–French 3-Factor
items.desc: Adds size (SMB) and value (HML) factors on top of CAPM's market factor.

items.name: Fama–French 5-Factor
items.desc: Further adds profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA) factors.

items.name: APT
items.desc: Multi-factor pricing without CAPM's market-equilibrium assumptions.

items.name: IPCA
items.desc: Latent-factor model in which factor loadings are instrumented by observable firm characteristics.

items.name: Autoencoder Asset Pricing
items.desc: A neural autoencoder learns nonlinear factor exposures directly from returns and characteristics (Gu–Kelly–Xiu).
items.used_by: related to → PRAGMA-style banking-event foundation models

title: Risk Measures
desc: Turning a return distribution into a single number a risk desk can act on.

items.name: Value-at-Risk (VaR)
items.desc: The loss that will not be exceeded with a given confidence level over a given horizon.

items.name: Historical Simulation VaR
items.desc: Nonparametric VaR read directly off the empirical distribution of past returns.

items.name: Parametric (Variance–Covariance) VaR
items.desc: Assumes normally distributed returns; fast, but understates tail risk.

items.name: Conditional VaR / Expected Shortfall
items.desc: The average loss beyond the VaR threshold; a coherent risk measure VaR itself is not.

items.name: Monte Carlo VaR
items.desc: Simulates thousands of price paths to build the loss distribution directly.

items.name: Extreme Value Theory (GPD)
items.desc: Models the tail of the loss distribution directly via the Generalized Pareto Distribution.

items.name: Copula-based Risk Models
items.desc: Models the joint dependence between assets separately from each asset's own marginal distribution.

title: Portfolio Optimization
desc: Turning return and risk estimates into position sizes.

items.name: Markowitz Mean–Variance
items.desc: The original efficient frontier: maximise return for a given level of variance.

items.name: Black–Litterman
items.desc: Blends market-equilibrium returns with an investor's subjective views via Bayesian updating.

items.name: Risk Parity
items.desc: Allocates so each asset contributes equally to portfolio risk, not equally to capital.

items.name: Kelly Criterion
items.desc: Optimal bet-sizing to maximise the long-run geometric growth rate of capital.

items.name: CVaR Optimization
items.desc: Rockafellar–Uryasev formulation minimising tail risk directly, solvable as a linear program.

items.name: Hierarchical Risk Parity
items.desc: Uses hierarchical clustering on the correlation matrix, avoiding unstable matrix inversion.

title: Credit Risk Models
desc: Estimating the probability and cost of a counterparty defaulting.

items.name: Merton Structural Model
items.desc: Treats equity as a call option on firm assets to infer default probability.

items.name: KMV Model
items.desc: Commercial extension of Merton estimating a market-implied ‘distance to default’.

items.name: Logistic Regression Scorecard
items.desc: The classical statistical credit-scoring model for probability of default.

items.name: CreditMetrics
items.desc: Portfolio credit-risk framework built on rating transition (migration) matrices.

items.name: Reduced-Form (Intensity) Models
items.desc: Models default as a jump process with a hazard rate, rather than an asset-value trigger.

title: Classical Machine Learning
desc: Supervised tabular models for direction, return and default prediction.

items.name: Linear / Logistic Regression
items.desc: Baseline parametric models for return magnitude or price-direction prediction.

items.name: k-Nearest Neighbours
items.desc: Predicts by similarity to the most comparable historical market states.

items.name: Support Vector Machines
items.desc: Margin-maximising classifier or regressor, common for price-direction prediction.

items.name: Decision Trees (CART)
items.desc: Interpretable rule-based splits over market and fundamental features.

items.name: Random Forest
items.desc: A bagged ensemble of decision trees; a robust baseline for tabular financial data.

items.name: Gradient Boosting (XGBoost / LightGBM / CatBoost)
items.desc: Sequential boosting of weak learners; the dominant benchmark for tabular financial features.

title: Unsupervised Outlier Methods
desc: Flag the point that doesn't belong, without ever being shown a labelled anomaly.

items.name: Isolation Forest
items.desc: Isolates points by random partitioning; anomalies need far fewer splits to isolate.

items.name: Local Outlier Factor
items.desc: Flags points whose local density is much lower than their neighbours'.

items.name: One-Class SVM
items.desc: Learns a boundary around normal data; anything outside it is scored anomalous.

items.name: DBSCAN
items.desc: Density-based clustering; points left in low-density regions are labelled outliers.

items.name: Elliptic Envelope
items.desc: Fits a robust covariance estimate and flags points outside the resulting ellipsoid.

items.name: Deep Isolation Forest
items.desc: Replaces axis-aligned splits with random neural-network projections for high-dimensional data.

title: Sequential Deep Learning
desc: Neural architectures built to carry information forward through time.

items.name: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)
items.desc: The base recurrent architecture for sequential and time-series data.

items.name: LSTM
items.desc: Gated RNN that solves the vanishing-gradient problem over long sequences.

items.name: GRU
items.desc: A simplified LSTM variant with fewer parameters and comparable performance.

items.name: Seq2Seq (Encoder–Decoder)
items.desc: Maps an input sequence to an output sequence, e.g. multi-step forecasting.

items.name: CNN-LSTM Hybrid
items.desc: Convolutional feature extraction feeding a recurrent temporal model.

items.name: ConvLSTM
items.desc: Convolutional gates inside the LSTM cell; captures joint spatial–temporal structure.

title: Attention & Transformer Models
desc: Self-attention replacing recurrence — the current state of the art for long financial sequences.

items.name: Transformer
items.desc: Self-attention over the full sequence; the base architecture behind every model below.

items.name: Informer
items.desc: Sparse ProbSparse attention for efficient long-sequence time-series forecasting.

items.name: Autoformer
items.desc: Decomposition plus auto-correlation, replacing standard self-attention for trend and seasonality.

items.name: FEDformer
items.desc: Frequency-domain (Fourier/Wavelet) enhanced Transformer; a strong recent benchmark on S&P 500 / NASDAQ series.

items.name: Anomaly Transformer
items.desc: Flags anomalies via the discrepancy between local and global attention patterns.

items.name: Temporal Fusion Transformer
items.desc: Interpretable multi-horizon forecasting combining LSTM, attention and variable-selection gates.

title: Autoencoders & Representation Learning
desc: Learn what ‘normal’ compresses to; large reconstruction error is the anomaly signal.

items.name: Vanilla Autoencoder
items.desc: Reconstruction-error anomaly scoring over tabular market features.

items.name: LSTM-Autoencoder
items.desc: Sequence-to-sequence reconstruction for time-series anomaly detection.

items.name: Variational Autoencoder
items.desc: A probabilistic latent space; anomaly score combines reconstruction error and KL-divergence.

items.name: Convolutional Autoencoder
items.desc: A 1-D convolutional encoder/decoder over price-and-volume windows.

items.name: Denoising / Sparse Autoencoder
items.desc: Trained to reconstruct clean data from corrupted input, forcing more robust features.

items.name: Transformer Autoencoder for Order Books
items.desc: Reconstructs limit-order-book sub-sequences to flag trade-based manipulation.

title: Generative Models
desc: Learn the data-generating process itself; a sample the model can't explain is the anomaly.

items.name: GAN
items.desc: A generator/discriminator pair; the discriminator's failure to tell real from fake flags anomalies.

items.name: TimeGAN
items.desc: A GAN framework explicitly preserving temporal dynamics for realistic synthetic financial series.

items.name: TAnoGAN
items.desc: GAN-based anomaly detector using the generator's reconstruction loss on time-series windows.

items.name: GAN-LSTM Hybrid
items.desc: An LSTM-based generator and discriminator; a strong recent benchmark for sequential anomaly detection.

items.name: Diffusion Models for Time Series
items.desc: Iterative denoising generative process; an emerging alternative to GANs for synthetic market data.

title: Graph-Based Models
desc: Assets, accounts and counterparties as nodes — the anomaly is in the structure, not just one series.

items.name: Graph Neural Network
items.desc: Propagates information across nodes connected by edges such as correlation or transaction flow.

items.name: Graph Attention Network
items.desc: A GNN variant that weighs each neighbour's contribution via a learned attention score.

items.name: Graph Autoencoder
items.desc: Reconstructs an adjacency or correlation matrix; a large error flags a structural anomaly.

items.name: GNN + Transformer Hybrids
items.desc: Combine relational (graph) and temporal (attention) structure for systemic anomaly discovery.

title: Fuzzy Logic & Neuro-Fuzzy Systems
desc: Where the boundary between ‘normal’ and ‘anomalous’ is itself uncertain, not just the data.

items.name: Fuzzy C-Means Clustering
items.desc: Soft clustering: each point holds partial membership across several risk clusters at once.

items.name: ANFIS
items.desc: Fuzzy if-then rules whose parameters are tuned by neural-network gradient learning.

items.name: Fuzzy Rule-Based Fraud Scoring
items.desc: Clusters financial and non-financial variables into fraud-risk categories for expert review.

items.name: Fuzzy Semi-Supervised Outlier Detection
items.desc: Treats volatility-outlier detection as fuzzy classification rather than hard-threshold regression.

items.name: Genetic-Fuzzy Hybrids
items.desc: Evolutionary algorithms tune fuzzy-rule and attention parameters jointly.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Markets
desc: Learning a trading or hedging policy from trial, error and reward — not from a labelled dataset.

items.name: Q-Learning
items.desc: Tabular value-based RL for simple, discrete trading-action policies.

items.name: Deep Q-Network
items.desc: Neural-network Q-function approximation for higher-dimensional market states.

items.name: Policy Gradient / REINFORCE
items.desc: Directly optimises a stochastic trading policy via gradient ascent on expected return.

items.name: Proximal Policy Optimization
items.desc: A stable, clipped policy-gradient method common in modern portfolio-management RL.

items.name: Actor–Critic (A2C/A3C)
items.desc: Combines a policy (actor) with a value estimator (critic) for lower-variance training.

items.name: DDPG
items.desc: An actor–critic method for continuous action spaces, e.g. position sizing.

title: Market Microstructure Models
desc: What happens inside the order book, tick by tick.

items.name: Kyle's Lambda
items.desc: Models the price impact of informed order flow; the classical price-impact benchmark.

items.name: Glosten–Milgrom Model
items.desc: Models the bid–ask spread as compensation for adverse selection from informed traders.

items.name: Hawkes Process
items.desc: A self-exciting point process: one trade raises the likelihood of the next, in clusters.

items.name: Autoregressive Conditional Duration
items.desc: Models the time between trade arrivals rather than the price level itself.

items.name: Limit Order Book Simulation
items.desc: Agent-based or statistical reconstruction of order-book dynamics for stress-testing detectors.

title: Regime-Switching & State-Space Models
desc: The market's own statistical rules change over time; these models let the rules switch too.

items.name: Hidden Markov Model
items.desc: A latent discrete regime — bull, bear, high-volatility — drives the observed returns.

items.name: Markov-Switching GARCH
items.desc: Combines regime-switching with conditional heteroskedasticity.

items.name: Particle Filter
items.desc: A nonlinear, non-Gaussian extension of the Kalman filter via sequential sampling.

items.name: Change-Point Detection (CUSUM, Bayesian Online)
items.desc: Flags a structural break in a series' statistical properties in real time.

title: Stochastic Processes for Derivatives
desc: Pricing the contracts written on top of the underlying market.

items.name: Black–Scholes–Merton
items.desc: Closed-form option pricing under geometric Brownian motion.

items.name: Binomial / Trinomial Trees
items.desc: Discrete-time lattice approximations for American and exotic option pricing.

items.name: Heston Model
items.desc: A stochastic-volatility extension of Black–Scholes that captures the volatility smile.

items.name: Jump-Diffusion (Merton, Kou)
items.desc: Adds discontinuous price jumps on top of the continuous diffusion process.

items.name: Monte Carlo Option Pricing
items.desc: Simulates many price paths to price path-dependent and exotic derivatives.

title: Fixed-Income & Term-Structure Models
desc: Modelling the shape of the yield curve and how it moves.

items.name: Vasicek Model
items.desc: A mean-reverting short-rate model; the classical one-factor term-structure benchmark.

items.name: CIR Model
items.desc: A Vasicek variant that guarantees non-negative interest rates.

items.name: Nelson–Siegel / Svensson
items.desc: A parsimonious parametric fit to the entire yield curve at once.

items.name: Hull–White Model
items.desc: Extends Vasicek with a time-dependent drift, fitting the current curve exactly.

title: Sentiment & NLP-Based Models
desc: Turning unstructured text — news, filings, social feeds — into a market signal.

items.name: Lexicon-Based Sentiment Scoring
items.desc: Dictionary-driven polarity scores extracted from news or social-media text.

items.name: Latent Dirichlet Allocation
items.desc: Unsupervised topic modelling to surface emerging narrative risk themes.

items.name: FinBERT / Financial Transformers
items.desc: Domain-fine-tuned language models for sentence-level market-sentiment classification.

items.name: Event-Study NLP Signals
items.desc: Extracts structured event tags — earnings surprise, guidance cut — from unstructured filings.

title: Explainability & Interpretability
desc: Once a model flags something, someone has to be able to say why.

items.name: SHAP
items.desc: Game-theoretic feature attribution that works for any black-box prediction.

items.name: LIME
items.desc: Fits a simple local surrogate model to explain one individual prediction.

items.name: Attention-Weight Visualization
items.desc: Inspects a Transformer's attention map to see which time-steps drove a flag.

items.name: DIFFI for Isolation Forest
items.desc: Depth-based feature-importance scoring specific to isolation-forest anomaly detectors.

title: Model Validation & Backtesting
desc: A model that looks great on history and fails live almost always failed here first.

items.name: Walk-Forward Split
items.desc: A chronological train/test split that respects the arrow of time and avoids look-ahead bias.

items.name: Purged / Embargoed k-Fold CV
items.desc: A cross-validation variant that removes leakage from overlapping financial-label windows.

items.name: White's Reality Check / SPA Test
items.desc: Statistical tests correcting for data-snooping bias across many backtested strategies.

items.name: Deflated Sharpe Ratio
items.desc: Adjusts the Sharpe ratio for the number of trials run and for non-normal returns.

items.name: Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation
items.desc: Generates many realistic backtest paths from a single dataset (López de Prado).

title: Systemic Risk & Network Models
desc: Risk that lives in the connections between institutions, not inside any one of them.

items.name: Network Centrality Measures
items.desc: Degree, eigenvector and betweenness centrality flag systemically important nodes.

items.name: DebtRank
items.desc: Models cascading distress propagation through a network of interbank exposures.

items.name: CoVaR
items.desc: The system's VaR conditional on one given institution being in distress.

items.name: Marginal Expected Shortfall
items.desc: A firm's expected loss conditional on a systemic market-wide downturn.

items.name: Antibenford Subgraphs
items.desc: Flags financial-network subgraphs whose transaction digits violate Benford's Law.

title: Fraud & Market-Manipulation Detection
desc: Named patterns regulators specifically look for, rather than generic statistical outliers.

items.name: Wash-Trading Detection
items.desc: Pattern-matching for self-dealing trades that transfer no genuine economic risk.

items.name: Spoofing / Layering Detection
items.desc: Flags large orders placed and cancelled with no intent to execute, to move the mid-price.

items.name: Pump-and-Dump Pattern Detection
items.desc: Detects the volume-and-price signature of coordinated promotion-then-sell schemes.

items.name: Benford's Law Digit Analysis
items.desc: Flags transaction datasets whose leading-digit distribution deviates from the expected law.

title: Alternative Data & Feature Engineering
desc: What actually feeds the model, upstream of the architecture itself.

items.name: Technical Indicators (RSI, MACD, Bollinger)
items.desc: Classical rule-based features still widely used as inputs to ML models.

items.name: Order-Flow Imbalance
items.desc: Net buy-versus-sell pressure from the order book as a short-horizon predictive feature.

items.name: Satellite / Geospatial Data
items.desc: Parking-lot counts or shipping traffic as alternative predictors of company activity.

items.name: Web-Scraped & App-Usage Signals
items.desc: Search trends, app downloads and job postings as leading indicators.

title: Hyperparameter & Architecture Search
desc: Tuning the model that tunes the market.

items.name: Grid / Random Search
items.desc: The baseline systematic and stochastic approaches to hyperparameter search.

items.name: Bayesian Optimization
items.desc: Models the hyperparameter response surface to search more efficiently than grid or random search.

items.name: Genetic Algorithms
items.desc: Evolutionary search over hyperparameters or fuzzy-rule structures.

items.name: Particle Swarm Optimization
items.desc: A swarm-based metaheuristic common in neuro-fuzzy and portfolio-weight tuning.

title: Evaluation Metrics
desc: How to know whether any of the above actually worked.

items.name: Sharpe / Sortino Ratio
items.desc: Risk-adjusted return measured against total volatility or downside volatility only.

items.name: Precision / Recall / F1
items.desc: Standard classification metrics, critical for reading imbalanced anomaly-detection results.

items.name: AUROC vs AUPRC
items.desc: ROC can mislead on imbalanced fraud data; AUPRC is the more reliable metric there.

items.name: Calmar Ratio / Max Drawdown
items.desc: Return measured against the worst peak-to-trough loss the strategy suffered.

items.name: F-beta / F4 Metric
items.desc: Weights recall over precision when missing a manipulation costs more than a false alarm.
